description: M3 idempotency exactly per design §11: insert-key-first inside the transfer transaction, replay detected only by the UNIQUE(user_id,key) violation (never SELECT an in_progress key), two-case semantics (committed -> replay saved response; rolled back -> no key persists, re-execute), body-hash mismatch -> 422, missing key on the three money POSTs -> 400. Depends on FEAT-003 (transferService + routes + money.canonicalJson/sha256 from FEAT-001).
steps: Create src/http/idempotency.ts: middleware/helper for the three money-mutating POSTs (POST /wallets/{id}/top-up, POST /transfers, POST /wallets/{id}/withdraw) that requires a valid UUID Idempotency-Key header -> missing/invalid raises 400 MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY. It computes body_hash = sha256Hex(canonicalJson(body)) (from FEAT-001). The other POSTs (/users, /users/{id}/wallets, /statement/ask, /admin/*) do NOT carry a key.

Extend transferService (the FEAT-003 seam, design §9.1 step 3) to insert the idempotency key FIRST inside the txn: INSERT INTO idempotency_keys(user_id,key,body_hash,status) VALUES (u,k,hash,'in_progress'). Resolve u per design §9.1/§11: peer_transfer -> owner of from_wallet_id; top_up/withdraw -> accounts.user_id of the path wallet (reject 400/404 if that path wallet is a system account, before inserting the key). On UNIQUE(user_id,key) violation -> replay path (do NOT proceed to move money).

Implement replay semantics (design §11.2): on the UNIQUE violation, the existing row is read; if status='completed' and body_hash matches -> return the saved response_code + response_body byte-for-byte, no money moves; if completed and body_hash differs -> 422 IDEMPOTENCY_BODY_MISMATCH, no money moves. On successful commit, update the key to status='completed' with the saved response_code and response_body (JSONB). On rollback (e.g. insufficient funds) the uncommitted key row disappears with the txn (Case 2) so a later same-key retry re-executes. Do NOT add any code path that SELECTs an in_progress key to branch on.
Wire the idempotency middleware into the three money routes so a missing key is rejected at 400 before any DB work, and the computed body_hash flows into transferService.

Create test/integration/idempotency.test.ts covering AC-2 (same successful request x5 sequential -> exactly 1 transfer, 5 byte-identical responses), AC-3 (same key x10 parallel via Promise.all -> exactly 1 transfer), AC-4 (same key + different amount -> 422 IDEMPOTENCY_BODY_MISMATCH, balances unchanged), AC-5 (a money POST without the header -> 400 MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY, plus a companion assertion that an exempt POST like /admin/transfers/{id}/release does NOT 400 for a missing key), and the §11.3 Case-2 sequence (first same-key attempt fails on insufficient funds and persists no key, top up, retry same key -> succeeds and creates a transfer).
acceptance_criteria: Against a real Postgres: AC-2 (5 identical responses, 1 transfer), AC-3 (10 parallel -> exactly 1 transfer), AC-4 (422 + no money moved), AC-5 (400 missing key; exempt POST not 400), and the Case-2 retry all pass.
No code path SELECTs an in_progress key to make a replay decision; replay is detected solely by the UNIQUE violation.
verification: If Postgres reachable: npm run migrate then npx vitest run test/integration/idempotency.test.ts -> pass (idempotency is a STEP-4 acceptance test).
If no Postgres in-environment: record in findings that idempotency integration tests were authored but NOT executed (no Postgres); keep tsc clean. Do NOT fabricate a pass.
findings:
COMPLETED (code + tests authored and typecheck-verified; Postgres-dependent idempotency integration tests AUTHORED but NOT executed — no Postgres/Docker in this environment).

WHAT WAS IMPLEMENTED (design §8 'Idempotency scope', §9.1 step 3+11, §11.1/11.2/11.3):
1. src/http/idempotency.ts — `requireIdempotency` Express middleware for the THREE money POSTs. Requires a valid UUID `Idempotency-Key` header; missing/invalid -> AppError('MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY') (400) via next(err), BEFORE any DB work. Computes bodyHash = sha256Hex(canonicalJson(req.body)) using the FEAT-001 helpers in money/money.ts. Stashes { key, bodyHash } on req.idempotency. Exports RequestIdempotency type. The exempt POSTs (/users, /users/{id}/wallets, /statement/ask, /admin/*) are NOT wired to this middleware and carry no key.
2. src/http/types.ts — extended the Express.Request augmentation with optional `idempotency?: { key; bodyHash }` (inlined to avoid a circular import with idempotency.ts).
3. src/services/transferService.ts — the FEAT-003 seam is now LIVE (method EXTENDED, not rewritten; §9.1 step order and the FEAT-005 fraud seam untouched):
   - insertIdempotencyKeyFirst(client, idempotency): STEP 3, the FIRST in-txn write — INSERT INTO idempotency_keys(user_id,key,body_hash,status) VALUES (u,k,hash,'in_progress'). On SQLSTATE 23505 (the UNIQUE(user_id,key) violation) it throws an internal `IdempotencyConflict` sentinel which aborts the txn (so NO money moves and, on rollback, no key persists).
   - Replay is detected SOLELY by that unique violation. NO code path SELECTs an in_progress key to branch on. After the txn rolls back, executeTransfer calls resolveReplay(pool, idempotency) which reads the COMMITTED conflicting row ON THE POOL: status='completed' + body_hash matches -> return saved { response_code, response_body } byte-for-byte (no money moves); body_hash differs -> AppError('IDEMPOTENCY_BODY_MISMATCH') (422); a non-completed/absent row (winner rolled back, Case 2) -> re-throw IdempotencyConflict so executeTransfer RE-EXECUTES from scratch (bounded by MAX_IDEMPOTENCY_ATTEMPTS=50 as a safety net; progress is guaranteed because a conflict only recurs when the prior winner did not commit a response).
   - completeIdempotencyKey(client, idempotency, response): STEP 11, inside the SAME txn — UPDATE idempotency_keys SET status='completed', response_code=$, response_body=$::jsonb WHERE user_id=$ AND key=$ AND body_hash=$. So the saved response and the money commit (or roll back) atomically together (§11.2 Case 1 vs Case 2).
   - user_id resolution per §9.1/§11 is done in the ROUTES (owner of from_wallet_id for peer_transfer; path wallet's accounts.user_id for top_up/withdraw; a system path wallet is rejected 404 by resolveUserWallet BEFORE the key insert) and passed in via IdempotencyContext.userId.
   - New types: TransferResponse { code; body }, TransferOutcome = { kind:'executed'; result; response? } | { kind:'replay'; response }. IdempotencyContext gained userId/key/bodyHash + a buildResponse(result)=>TransferResponse callback so the EXACT route body (incl. the first request's request_id) is built and persisted at step 11 and replayed byte-for-byte (satisfies AC-2's 5 byte-identical bodies and §11.2 'byte-for-byte').
   - executeTransfer return type CHANGED from Promise<TransferResult> to Promise<TransferOutcome>. Only the three money routes call it; all updated (see below).
4. src/http/routes/wallets.ts + transfers.ts — wired `requireIdempotency` as per-route middleware on the three money POSTs (runs before the handler, so a missing key 400s before DB work). Each handler resolves the owner user_id, passes idempotency { userId, key, bodyHash, buildResponse } into executeTransfer, and sends outcome.response verbatim (status+body) for both executed and replay outcomes (a replay is byte-identical to the first response). walletsRouter adds walletTransferBody + sendOutcome helpers; transfersRouter adds transferBody.
5. test/integration/idempotency.test.ts — all through the REAL HTTP app (app.listen(0) + fetch), guarded by describe.skipIf(SKIP_INTEGRATION):
   - AC-2: 5 sequential same-key top-ups -> all 201, all 5 response bodies byte-identical (raw text compare), exactly 1 transfer, balance moved once.
   - AC-3: 10 parallel same-key top-ups via Promise.all -> all 201, single distinct body, exactly 1 transfer, one movement.
   - AC-4: same key + different amount -> 422 IDEMPOTENCY_BODY_MISMATCH, balance unchanged, still 1 transfer.
   - AC-5: a money POST (top-up) with NO Idempotency-Key -> 400 MISSING_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY (and a non-UUID key also -> 400), no money moved / no transfer; companion assertion that an EXEMPT POST (POST /users/{id}/wallets) does NOT 400 for a missing key.
   - §11.3 Case-2: a peer transfer with an unfunded sender fails 422 INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS and persists NO idempotency key (asserted via idempotency_keys lookup); after a top-up, retrying the SAME key succeeds (201 COMPLETED), the key now exists, and exactly one peer transfer was created.

AC-5 EXEMPT-POST NOTE: the task example named `/admin/transfers/{id}/release` as the exempt companion, but the /admin/* routes do not exist until FEAT-005. The test instead uses the already-existing exempt POST /users/{id}/wallets to assert an exempt POST does NOT 400 for a missing key — same invariant, in-scope for FEAT-004. A FEAT-005/convergence step may add the admin-release companion assertion once that route lands.

STAMPEDE ORDERING NOTE (for the convergence/fixer step): test/integration/stampede.test.ts (FEAT-003) sends non-UUID Idempotency-Key headers (`stampede-${iter}-${i}`). Now that requireIdempotency enforces a valid UUID, those requests would 400 instead of exercising the withdraw path, so the stampede test as written will FAIL against a real Postgres until its keys are changed to valid UUIDs (e.g. randomUUID() per request). This was flagged (not fixed) because it is FEAT-003's test and outside FEAT-004's scope; it needs exactly 100 DISTINCT UUIDs per iteration to preserve the 50-winners assertion. tsc is unaffected (string literals typecheck fine); this only bites at real-Postgres run time.
